The bat is evasive (flying), gains life, exiles a card from opponent's hand, and applies pressure while they can't attack with their summoning-sick Drowner. Passing (leaf 0) is passive in a race—I'd let them develop answers while I hold creatures. Playing Swamp (leaf 4) wastes my turn; I already have sufficient mana and should be deploying threats now to pressure their board.

Island and Swamp are already tapped from casting the Deep-Cavern Bat, so I can't tap them again. My hand has 2 more bats and a Swamp, but I lack the mana to cast another bat ({1}{B} cost with only {U} or {B} available). Passing ends my main phase so I can move to combat.

I have no legal attacks this turn: Floodpits Drowner is tapped, Deep-Cavern Bat is summoning sick (can block but not attack), and Restless Reef is a land (not a creature unless I activate {2}{U}{B}, which I can't afford). Go for the Throat is tempting as removal denial, but Kaito is the single most threatening card available to them.

I already have sufficient mana to cast my bats; the extra land doesn't justify deferring threats in a tempo game where I need to race.

Blocking with Deep-Cavern Bat is significantly better. While we lose our creature and its hand disruption, we: (1) eliminate Floodpits Drowner, a 2/1 threat with vigilance that would attack repeatedly untapped, (2) gain 1 life from lifelink (21 vs 18), improving our life total, and (3) still have another Deep-Cavern Bat in hand to rebuild disruption next turn. Taking 2 unblocked damage to preserve a single point of disruption is poor tempo when eliminating a recurring threat. Blocking optimizes for both life gain and threat removal in the mirror match.

Pass priority. End of combat phase has no relevant actions for me. My lands are tapped and there are no instant-speed interactions. Moving into opponent's end step and then my turn.

Preacher of the Schism (option 3) is strongest: a 2/4 with deathtouch creates a strong clock and draws cards when we're at life parity. While tapping out is risky, in a mirror match we need to deploy threats efficiently to pressure the opponent before they stabilize. Deep-Cavern Bat (option 1, score 70) is solid as it provides disruption and keeps mana up for responses, but Preacher's superior stats and card draw potential outweigh the tempo cost in this position. Playing a land (option 2) is too passive for a tempo-focused matchup. Passing (option 0) concedes tempo when we should be applying pressure.

Playing the Swamp is clearly correct. I have one land play per turn and no downside to using it—the Swamp expands my mana base from 3 to 4 lands, giving me an untapped land for future turns. All my current lands are tapped after casting Preacher, so I have no mana to spend this turn anyway. Playing the land advances my position without any cost and is a free resource. Passing and leaving the Swamp in hand wastes a land drop opportunity that won't return until next turn.

Passing (Option 1) leaves me with only Preacher of the Schism (2/4) against opponent's Deep-Cavern Bat and Kaito, maintaining board disadvantage while I have mana available—a missed opportunity to develop threats. Activating Restless Reef's ability (Option 2) immediately generates a 4/4 deathtouch creature, transforming my board presence from 1 threat to 2 strong ones (Reef + Preacher). The 4/4 deathtouch is formidable against opponent's small creatures and can attack for 4 damage this turn or provide excellent defense. Despite using all my mana and tapping Restless Reef, this develops critical tempo and board parity. The deathtouch ability severely limits opponent's attack/block options, making Option 2 significantly superior for controlling the game state.

Both options show opponent at 0 life, suggesting both lead to victory, but they differ in execution. Attack-none (Option 0) is passive and keeps creatures untapped for defense, but fails to develop immediate threats or leverage the kill potential. Attack-all (Option 1) is strongly favored because: (1) Restless Reef's attack ability mills opponent for 4 cards per attack, potentially triggering mill-out if opponent's library is depleted; (2) Attacking with Restless Reef (4/4 deathtouch) and Preacher (2/4 deathtouch) forces opponent to block or take 6 damage—if opponent blocks with Kaito, either creature's deathtouch kills it; (3) This removes opponent's most dangerous threat while dealing damage or progressing the mill-out win. The aggressive line completes the win faster and more decisively than the passive option.

At 14 life facing flying threats (Deep-Cavern Bat 1/1, Enduring Curiosity 4/3), I must address the board rather than remain passive. Option 1 (Pass) at 35: Keeps mana untapped but does nothing to address Enduring Curiosity and Deep-Cavern Bat—passive play when I'm low on life is dangerous. Option 2 (Cast Cut Down) at 50: Removes Deep-Cavern Bat efficiently ({B} cost), but Enduring Curiosity (4/3, total power+toughness 7) survives Cut Down and remains a dangerous flyer drawing cards each time it damages me—partial solution leaving the bigger threat. Option 3 (Activate Restless Reef) at 72: Get a 4/4 deathtouch creature that blocks Enduring Curiosity effectively (Curiosity's 3 damage is lethal due to deathtouch), removes the key threat, and applies pressure immediately. Although this uses all available mana and taps Restless Reef, the immediate strong defense is critical at low life. Option 3 is optimal for stabilizing and controlling flying threats.

At 14 life, both options maintain the same defensive posture with Restless Reef 4/4 ready to block or attack. Option 1 (Pass) at 47: Fails to play an available land drop; in Magic, playing lands that don't create immediate disadvantage is nearly always correct, and passing leaves resources unused. Option 2 (Play Darkslick Shores) at 53: Follows the fundamental principle of maximizing mana development—Darkslick Shores enters tapped but expands my mana base for future turns, enabling Deep-Cavern Bat casting ({1}{B}) or other spells when needed. While the immediate board impact is neutral (both options leave me at 14 life with identical creature positioning), playing the land is slightly superior for long-term resource management and keeps options open. At 14 life, I'm unlikely to win quickly, so building mana efficiency for future turns is prudent.

Both options lead to opponent at 0 life (game-ending state), but they differ significantly in method. Attack-none (Option 0) at 55: Passive approach that keeps Preacher untapped for defense but fails to develop immediate threats or leverage Restless Reef's milling ability. At 14 life, a passive strategy invites the opponent to stabilize or find answers. Attack-all (Option 1) at 92: Strongly favored. Attacking with Restless Reef (4/4 deathtouch) and Preacher (2/4 deathtouch) for 6 damage forces opponent's hand—if unblocked, substantial life loss occurs; if blocked, deathtouch trades favorably. Critically, Restless Reef's attack triggers milling ("Whenever {this} attacks, target player mills four cards"), progressing toward mill-out win condition. At 14 life, I'm low enough that aggressive tempo is essential. Attack-all maximizes damage output, activates mill synergy, and presses the advantage decisively.

At 3 life facing opponent's Deep-Cavern Bat (1/1 T), Enduring Curiosity (4/3 T), Kaito (tapped), and Preacher of the Schism (2/4 untapped, summoning sick), every option is dire—I'm in a race against a superior board position. Option 1 (Pass) at 8: Passive approach guarantees I face untapped flying threats (Enduring Curiosity 4/3 + Kaito 3/4+ = 7+ damage unblocked) next turn and die with 3 life. Option 2 (Cast Cut Down) at 15: Removes only Deep-Cavern Bat (1/1, the sole target ≤5 total power+toughness); Enduring Curiosity (4/3=7) and Kaito both survive, still dealing lethal unblocked damage next turn. Option 3 (Activate Restless Reef) at 35: Best emergency survival—generates a 4/4 deathtouch blocker to absorb damage from Enduring Curiosity, mitigating 4 damage and extending survival one additional turn when facing near-certain death. At 3 life with no creatures, defensive stabilization via Restless Reef is the only path to a possible comeback, though the position remains critical.

At 3 life, the untapped Restless Reef 4/4 is my only defense against opponent's flying threats. Option 1 (Pass) at 40: Maintains the untapped 4/4 blocker essential for survival—opponent's Enduring Curiosity (4/3) will attack next turn and the 4/4 can block it and survive (taking 3 damage but not dying to the creature). Keeping this defensive option open is critical at 3 life. Option 2 (Cast Cut Down) at 25: Removes Deep-Cavern Bat (1/1), a minor threat given the 4/3 Enduring Curiosity and 2/4 Preacher, but tapping Restless Reef compromises my defense—opponent attacks with Enduring Curiosity unblocked for 4 damage, I die at 3 life with -1 life total. Sacrificing the untapped blocker to remove a small flyer is severely disadvantageous when facing lethal attacks. The untapped 4/4 remains my sole stabilization path; losing it guarantees defeat next turn.

At 3 life with Restless Reef already as an untapped 4/4 creature, the decision mirrors the critical need for defense. Option 1 (Pass) at 42: Maintains untapped 4/4 blocker—when opponent attacks with Enduring Curiosity (4/3 tapped, will untap next turn), the 4/4 can block it and survive (takes 3 damage, dies to the 4/3 but trade is even for blocking). Keeping the creature untapped preserves defensive flexibility for opponent's next turn. Option 2 (Cast Cut Down) at 24: Removes Deep-Cavern Bat (1/1, minor threat) but taps Restless Reef, eliminating the untapped blocker—opponent then attacks with untapped Enduring Curiosity (4/3) for 4 unblocked damage to my 3 life, resulting in death. The cost of removing a small flying creature (1/1) is the loss of an essential defensive blocker against a much larger threat (4/3). At 3 life, the untapped 4/4 is the only stabilization tool; sacrificing it guarantees lethal attack next turn.

Option 2 (pass to combat) is stronger: Restless Reef has vigilance, so attacking doesn't tap it—I deal 4 damage to opponent (19 life) while maintaining my untapped blocker for Enduring Curiosity. This is critical at 3 life; I need to apply pressure while keeping defense intact. Option 1 (play Undercity Sewers) develops mana but doesn't leverage vigilance's advantage and doesn't address the lethal threat that requires speed.

Option 1 (Play Undercity Sewers) edges out Option 0 despite both paths leading to critical pressure. At 3 life with Restless Reef tapped (cannot block Enduring Curiosity's 4/3 flying next turn), the position is likely lost. However, playing the land: (1) develops mana base for future turns despite entering tapped, (2) uses the land drop efficiently, (3) keeps more options alive. Passing preserves 0 untapped blockers while staying at 0 active mana. Playing Undercity Sewers at least advances the game state, surveil 1 on entry, and potentially enables plays after the next untap step. Neither option solves the lethal threat, but the slight board development edge favors the active play.
